modes.bear: Heavy cash burn on demand generation delays profitability and strains unit economics amid fierce competition.
modes.bull: Aggressive spending drives rapid user acquisition and establishes category leadership in high-growth quick commerce markets.
modes.simple: Quick delivery startups are spending a lot of money to get more customers and beat their rivals, prioritizing growth over profits for now.

rows.summary: Quick commerce and instant delivery startups Snabbit, Swish, and FirstClub are deploying substantial capital to generate consumer demand and expand their market presence. This aggressive spending strategy reflects intense competition within the quick commerce and ultra-fast delivery sectors as players race for customer acquisition. For Indian retail investors, this trend highlights the high-burn nature of the quick commerce space, which continues to prioritize rapid scaling over immediate profitability.
rows.why_it_matters: High-burn competition continues in the quick commerce sector.
rows.winners_losers: Consumers gain / startup margins hurt
